audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer called levels 3 through 2+ items 'Skill' while the content layer and the packet chart both gave Cassiopeia levels 1-6 and Azir the last row. Five rows rendered two answers.
audit.why: Miasma grounds Shifting Sands, Twin Fang recasts every 0.75s and Noxious Blast every 3.5s at 850 range: the lane is hers until Azir's teamfight build arrives. Win rate is 48.72% for Azir, which fits a losing lane and a winning late game.
audit.corrected: Full layer moved to Cassiopeia for levels 3, 4-5, 6 and first item, and Azir for 2+ items, with each why rewritten to argue the same verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] and spikes[1].text put a 'Petrify range increase' at levels 4-5 and described level 6 as her ult getting bigger; spikes[3].text spiked on 'Shurelya's cooldown'.
audit.why: Petrifying Gaze is not available before level 6 (120/100/80s), and Azir's page builds Nashor's into Sorcerer's, Liandry's and Rabadon's — Shurelya's is a placeholder item.
audit.corrected: Level 6 stated as the arrival of Petrifying Gaze at 825 range; levels 4-5 stated as her Noxious Blast mana advantage; the late spike named against Rabadon's and Emperor's Divide.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text used the fabricated name 'Noxious Blight' for the grounding field and attributed it to the wrong slot; breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all.
audit.why: Riot's kit names her Q Noxious Blast; the grounding is Miasma (W), 24/22/20/18/16s, and grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities — which is exactly Azir's Shifting Sands. Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies FACING her and merely slows those with their backs turned, the single most actionable interaction in this matchup and it appeared nowhere.
audit.corrected: Miasma named as the ground, with its real cooldown; the facing rule for Petrifying Gaze written into the level 6 row; Twin Fang's 0.75s recast stated so the reader stops waiting for it to be down.
sources: brief enemyKit W/E/R text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned once, in a misgendered clause ('into his sustain'), and never tied to a timing.
audit.why: Twin Fang heals Cassiopeia for a percentage of damage dealt and recasts every 0.75s; the missing-interactions file flags this matchup as needs-antiheal.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds tied to the moment she is ahead and to the first-item row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cassiopeia is female and the page called her 'he/his' in tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, dosFull titles and bodies, loading, report[3], report[8] and report[9].
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists cassiopeia as female; the owner is addressed as 'you', so every third-person pronoun on this page refers to her.
audit.corrected: All affected strings rewritten in the feminine.

edits.after: Miasma is the grounding field: standing in it disables Shifting Sands, so she holds you in the poison and Twin Fangs you down.

edits.before: Petrify range and stun duration go up, letting her land a guaranteed follow-up Twin Fang burst that most mid laners can't escape.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze arrives at 825 range and stuns everyone facing her — turned away it only slows, so she opens with it from the front.

edits.before: Only at full build with Emperor's Divide and Shurelya's cooldown can you contest her in extended fights — otherwise she out-scales you all game.
edits.after: With Rabadon's up and Emperor's Divide banked you finally win the long fight: soldiers out-range Twin Fang and the wall cuts her off her target.

edits.before: Petrify range increase at this stage creates deadly stun-into-burst combos you can't escape

edits.before: Cassiopeia's Miasma denies you safe farming spots and grounds your Arise dash-ins, while Twin Fang scales off missing health to snowball any poke she lands — you're forced into a passive, soldier-poke-only lane where she keeps stacking free damage.
edits.after: Miasma grounds you, and grounded means Shifting Sands will not fire — so the cloud is not poke, it is a cage with a 24-second key. Farm through soldiers from behind your own sand, and never take a last-hit standing in poison she can Twin Fang.

edits.before: It isn't until Emperor's Divide is up alongside a second item spike that you can finally interrupt her Petrify setup or peel through her poison zone — full-build Azir with cooldowns available can just barely contest her scaling, but she remains dangerous in extended skirmishes.
edits.after: Two items in, the range war turns: soldiers hit from further than Twin Fang's 700 and Emperor's Divide throws her off whatever she is healing from. Fight her from the side or the back — Petrifying Gaze only stuns what is facing it, and she has no dash to fix her angle.

notes: Cassiopeia is female and the page was written with a male template: tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, two dosFull titles, dosFull[1].d, loading, report[8] and report[9] all said he/his. All corrected. 'Noxious Blight' was a fabricated name (real: Noxious Blast) and the grounding belongs to Miasma (W), which is now stated with its 24s cooldown and tied to Shifting Sands being disabled. The facing rule on Petrifying Gaze (stun only for enemies facing her, slow otherwise) was absent everywhere and is now in the level 6 row, the loading tip and the late-game text. Chart: full layer said Skill for rows 2-6 while content and the packet both said Cassiopeia 0-5 / Azir 6; aligned the full layer to that and rewrote each why to match. I did NOT touch phases[N].rating anywhere — see questionsForUser, the scale is inconsistent between files. Not asserted: whether Emperor's Divide interrupts Petrifying Gaze, whether the knockback moves her mid-cast, and whether soldiers block Twin Fang's projectile — none of that is in Riot's text.
